newsitem.title: USA: Mercury reduces debt principal, makes payments.
newsitem.headline: Mercury reduces debt principal, makes payments.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Tuesday it reached an agreement with creditors, under which Mercury made a $70 million payment to reduce the principal of its outstanding debt and brought its interest payments current.

The company also agreed, depending on cash flow, to make additional periodic payments to reduce principal. Creditors pledged not to take action against the company under their debt agreements prior to October 1, at which time the forbearance agreement may be renewed, Mercury said.
It now has $933.6 million of debt outstanding.

Mercury said its creditors granted an extension to September 30 of previously granted waivers, permitting the company to continue to pledge assets as collateral on its credit facility with the Bank of America. No funds are currently outstanding under the facility.
Mercury also said it released its 1996 balance sheet, reflecting year-end shareholders' equity of $168.9 million.
The company said the only significant difference with the April 23 estimate comes from a decision to book the loss from the Lyndon Insurance sale in 1997 rather than 1996.

The balance sheet was audited by independent public accountant Arthur Andersen LLP. In line with the company's disclosure on April 23, the auditor's opinion contains language questioning Mercury's ability to continue as a going concern.
The company said release of the income statement for the year has been delayed pending the resolution of timing issues related to recognition of revenues and expenses between 1995 and 1996.

The company has been engaged in informal discussions with the Securities and Exchange Commission and continues to work with Arthur Andersen LLP and KPMG Peat Marwick, its auditor for the years prior to 1996, to resolve allocation issues.
No date for the release of the income statements has been given.

"The audited balance sheet gives us a much-needed solid platform from which to address long-term financial solutions," Brandt said. "We are working closely with our creditors and our investment banker to explore various avenues aimed at reestablishing the company's financial footing."
The company said it expects to issue results from the first quarter of 1997 in about one week.
